question.worked_solution:
We can just take the constant factor out of the integral, and then apply the power rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{3}x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{2}{3}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(\frac{{x}^{1+1}}{1+1})+C \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$
